quote: spectral form

quote: raw affine level
preview: The raw affine level is the scalar multiplying the central current cocycle in the chosen invariant form, with long roots of squared length two. It is the shifted level minus the dual Coxeter number.

quote: adjunction unit and counit
preview: For a left adjoint F and right adjoint G, the unit compares an input X with GFX, and the counit evaluates FGY at Y. Their two triangle identities recover the original maps on FX and GY.

quote: centre of their algebra
preview: The centre of a unital associative algebra consists of the elements commuting with every algebra element. Multiplication by such elements gives exactly the natural endomorphisms of the identity on its left modules.

quote: pointed Heisenberg roof
preview: Here a pointed action roof keeps the exterior actor resolution, the admissible boundary equivalence and their commuting actions. Its unit comparison identifies the action of the actor’s unit with the identity on the boundary.

quote: normalized boundary hypothesis
preview: For the specified normalization, measure and puncture coordinates, the two four-point sewings converge in their channel discs. The marked channel vectors lie in the spectral L² spaces and are identified by the stated unitary fusion transformation.

quote: root jets
preview: In a fixed charge, a finite root jet is a linear functional on the shuffle coefficients that kills every root degree above some finite bound.

quote: correspondence and its orientation root
preview: A line on the moduli problem has tensor square equal to the self-extension determinant. Its joining maps include the cross determinant and must agree along flags of exact sequences.

quote: proper trace ideal
preview: On the two-term Hilbert complex the trace is defined on trace-class chain maps and trace-class homotopies. It is the difference of the component traces in degree zero and vanishes on boundaries.

quote: Prepare a superposition of these alternatives
preview: A superposition adds state vectors with complex amplitudes. Here the normalized sum and difference give the two occupations equal probabilities and opposite relative signs.

quote: Take the first two harmonics of a free current
preview: In the neutral level-one representation, creating a quantum of harmonic n multiplies a polynomial by pₙ. Removing one acts by n times differentiation with respect to pₙ.

quote: Adjointness gives
preview: Moving a creation mode from the first entry of the inner product to the second replaces it by the annihilation mode of the same harmonic. With vacuum norm one this fixes the norms of all occupation monomials.

quote: Which operation of the current measures this exchange?
preview: On the energy-two space, S interchanges the normalized occupations (2,0) and (0,1). Their normalized sum has eigenvalue +1 and their normalized difference has eigenvalue −1.

quote: One disk reading varies from sample to sample.
preview: For one disk sample, square the first harmonic amplitude, multiply by the conjugate of the second, and take twice the real part. Its mean agrees with the expectation of O = 2S, giving +2 in the sum preparation and −2 in the difference preparation.

quote: At higher energies one can join harmonics
preview: On a state of energy n, the cubic observable W sums the joins of i and j into i + j and their adjoint splits, with a factor ½ over ordered positive pairs satisfying i + j ≤ n. At energy two this gives the exchange S.

quote: with the singular terms removed by normal ordering
preview: For the neutral free current, normal ordering puts creation modes to the left of annihilation modes. For two currents this removes their double-pole contraction.

quote: Multiplying the ground-state wavefunction by the density wave
preview: The nth density wave is the sum of the nth Fourier phases of the measured particle positions on the ring. Multiplication by this sum adds n units of momentum, each of size 2πℏ/L on a ring of circumference L.

quote: the energy operator above the ground state acts on density-wave polynomials
phrase: energy operator above the ground state
preview: On a ring with an odd number N of free spinless fermions, the excitation energy on shell n acts as ε₁n + (2ε₁/N)W, where ε₁ is the first kinetic gap. Subtract ε₁n and divide by 2ε₁/N to read the cubic observable W.

quote: At every energy \(n\) the Schur polynomials
preview: For a partition λ with at most N rows, its Schur polynomial is the determinant of the shifted orbitals divided by the ground-state determinant of N fermions. Multiplying the ground state by this polynomial prepares the indicated occupied momenta.

quote: What function of \(x\) gives the mean of its readings?
preview: At fixed x, integrate the observable against the Gaussian weight in y and divide by the integral of that weight. The result is the conditional expectation as a function of x.

quote: is the conditional variance.
preview: At fixed x this is the conditional mean of y² minus the square of the conditional mean of y. For the quadratic action with b > 0 it equals ℏ/b.

quote: a Wilson line of charge
preview: An abelian Wilson line of charge a couples to the integral of the gauge one-form along its oriented path. For a ray directed into the half-space and vertical near its endpoint, the positively oriented contour integral of the current divided by 2πi gives a.

quote: A collar of Euclidean length
preview: A cylinder of length t propagates a holomorphic oscillator amplitude of energy m by the factor exp(−tm) after subtracting the vacuum energy. In the displayed pairing it acts on the second amplitude.

quote: a Laurent series in the separation
preview: On a fixed input state, a field gives a series in the separation with coefficients in the state space and only finitely many negative powers. The pole bound can change with the input.

quote: The bracket is skew-symmetric.
preview: The Beilinson–Drinfeld bracket is a skew binary operation on a right differential module. It accepts inputs with poles along the diagonal, takes values on the diagonal with normal derivatives, and satisfies Jacobi.

quote: On this labelled transverse slice
preview: At a collision the slice fixes each cluster’s position and varies the differences between its labelled points. The normal link is computed on the separated part of a small such slice with the given local coefficients.

quote: summing over consecutive cuts gives
preview: A cut after position p divides a word into its first p inputs and the remaining inputs. Its open set allows collisions within each block and requires different positions across the cut.

quote: For an associative chiral algebra in this word construction
preview: Here this is an augmented algebra associative up to coherent homotopies for consecutive-cut convolution, with augmentation ideal zero on the empty word. Its bar coproduct identifies the full word coefficient with the external product of the two block coefficients wherever the cut separates them.

quote: by a representation, or module,
preview: A left module is a vector space on which the algebra unit acts as the identity and the product ab acts by first applying b and then a.

quote: For an ordinary bialgebra \(H\), a coproduct
preview: For a bialgebra H, the coproduct is a coassociative unital algebra map from H to H ⊗ H. In each summand of Δ(h), the first factor acts on the first module and the second factor on the second module.

quote: A more general exchange requires a braiding
preview: A braiding is a natural isomorphism from M ⊗ N to N ⊗ M for each pair of objects. Its two hexagon identities describe how a single object crosses a tensor product on either side.

quote: so applying naturality to
preview: Applying the operator on M and then a module map f gives the same result as applying f and then the operator on N. The proof takes f to be right multiplication on the regular left module.

quote: modeled by the Hochschild cochain complex
preview: These are the derived bimodule maps from A to itself. For an ordinary algebra over a field, degree n of the bar model consists of multilinear maps from n copies of A to A.

quote: its absolute scalar or determinant line
preview: For a bounded finite-dimensional cochain complex, take the tensor product of the top exterior powers in even degrees and their duals in odd degrees. This one-dimensional space records how the normalization changes under a change of basis.

quote: a total-charge measurement gives
preview: For an additive charge, the generator acts on two systems by Q ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ Q. A product of charge eigenstates has the sum of their eigenvalues.

quote: representations of a given symmetry
preview: A representation assigns operators linearly to the elements of an algebra. The unit fixes every vector, and the product ab acts by applying b and then a.

quote: let \(S\) exchange \(a\) with \(b\)
preview: Here S is the operator interchanging the two unit occupation states at energy two. It acts on their span and squares to the identity.

quote: Evaluating the two action laws
preview: The unit fixes every vector, and acting by a product ab gives the same result as acting first by b and then by a. The proof tests both laws on the tensor of the two algebra units.

quote: Group associativity therefore gives coassociativity.
preview: Applying the coproduct to the first output of Δ or to its second output gives the same threefold tensor. On a group function this equality evaluates the function at the same product of three elements with either parenthesization.

quote: Group inversion also acts by pullback.
preview: Pulling a function back along a map means composing the function with that map. Pulling f back by group inversion gives g ↦ f(g⁻¹).

quote: this is expressed using the antipode
preview: The antipode S is the convolution inverse of the identity on a Hopf algebra. Multiplying the two outputs of the coproduct after applying S to either output gives the counit times the unit.

quote: on the dual, so evaluation sends
preview: The algebraic dual consists of all linear functionals on the module M. A Lie algebra element x acts on a functional φ by sending m to −φ(xm).

quote: every algebraic tensor gives a finite-rank operator
preview: An operator has finite rank if its image lies in a finite-dimensional subspace. A tensor ∑uᵢ ⊗ φᵢ sends v to ∑φᵢ(v)uᵢ, whose value lies in the span of the finitely many vectors uᵢ.

quote: The tensor product also acts on intertwiners.
preview: An intertwiner is a linear map between modules that commutes with the action of each algebra element. Transporting a state by that map before or after applying the same element gives the same vector.

quote: With parentheses identified by the associator
preview: The associator is the natural isomorphism from (L ⊗ M) ⊗ N to L ⊗ (M ⊗ N). For four objects the pentagon makes the two sequences of reassociations agree.

quote: give the two hexagons.
preview: One hexagon moves a single object past a pair, and the other moves a pair past a single object. Each requires agreement with the two successive crossings, after reassociation.

quote: some equalities are replaced by homotopies
preview: For degree-zero cochain maps f and g, a homotopy is a map h of degree −1 with f − g = d h + h d. The two terms use the differentials in the target and source, respectively.

quote: In the weak Hopf algebra reconstructed
preview: Here the reconstructed algebra has one endomorphism block for each simple Ising sector. Its coproduct is multiplicative, and Δ(1) projects a pair of junctions onto those whose intermediate sector labels match.

quote: also requires the marked braiding
preview: For the Ising lines the marking specifies the operator for an oriented half-exchange, including its phase on each fusion channel. The dimensions and fusion multiplicities alone leave these phases undetermined.

quote: The adjunction counit sends
preview: For the free-module and forgetful functors, this counit is the evaluation map A ⊗ U(M) → M. It sends a ⊗ m to the state obtained by acting with a on m.

quote: The coalgebra counit sends
preview: The counit ε sends an algebra element to its scalar action on the tensor unit. Applying ε to either output of the coproduct and identifying the scalar factor recovers the original element.

quote: The Laurent coefficient selected by that contour
preview: For a field A(z), the coefficient of z⁻ⁿ⁻¹ is the mode Aₙ. Its action on a fixed input is extracted by taking the residue of zⁿA(z) on that input.

quote: To measure the charge of a line ending on a surface
preview: For the abelian current, the charge of an endpoint state is its eigenvalue under the zero mode J₀. A positively oriented integral of the current around the endpoint, divided by 2πi, reads that eigenvalue.

quote: The field thus supplies a whole family of operations
preview: A field is a formal series of operators on the state space. On each input the result is a Laurent series with only finitely many negative powers, and the bound can vary with the state.

quote: On the vacuum all the positive modes vanish.
preview: On the neutral level-one polynomial representation, the positive mode Jₙ acts as n times differentiation with respect to pₙ for n > 0. It kills the constant vacuum polynomial.

quote: This is locality of order two.
preview: Multiplying the commutator of the two fields by (z − w)² kills it coefficient by coefficient on every input state. In this double-pole example one factor leaves the formal delta distribution.

quote: A vertex algebra makes this relation
preview: An even vertex algebra assigns pairwise local fields to states and has a vacuum and a translation operator. The vacuum field is the identity, Y(a,z) on the vacuum is regular with constant term a, and translation differentiates the fields.

quote: Creation gives
preview: The field of a state a, applied to the vacuum, gives a power series with constant term a. This supplies the initial value in the translation equation.

quote: relates the chiral bracket to the full operator product
preview: In the Beilinson–Drinfeld convention this is a skew binary operation satisfying Jacobi, with values supported on the diagonal. Its inputs allow Laurent multipliers, so residue tests can extract regular as well as singular coefficients.

quote: for the occupation inner product supplies
preview: At level one the vacuum has norm one, and a creation mode is adjoint to the annihilation mode of the same harmonic. The first two harmonics have orthogonal occupation monomials, with squared norm m! 2ⁿ n! for the monomial of exponents (m,n).

quote: the other expansion of the pole
preview: Reversing the radial order expands the double pole in nonnegative powers of z/w. Subtracting this expansion from the expansion in powers of w/z gives the w-derivative of the formal delta distribution.

quote: The normally ordered square prepares
preview: For the neutral current, subtract the double-pole contraction from J(z)J(w) in the indicated radial order and take the regular value at z = w. The resulting field prepares p₁² from the vacuum as its constant term.

quote: This particular two-point coefficient is
preview: Apply the two currents to the neutral vacuum with J(w) acting first, then take the constant coefficient in the occupation variables. With the vacuum functional normalized to one on the vacuum, the result is the expansion of κ/(z − w)² in powers of w/z.

quote: keep this nonzero numerical level fixed
preview: For m > 0 the commutator of Jₘ with J₋ₘ acts by the scalar km. The same k is the double-pole coefficient of two currents and stays fixed as the endpoint charge varies.

quote: project onto the oscillator-free outgoing state
preview: In the Fock module of total charge a + b, the outgoing state with no oscillators is represented by the constant polynomial 1. Projecting to it reads the constant coefficient in the oscillator variables.

quote: the central term to satisfy the Jacobi identity
preview: For any three Lie algebra elements the cyclic sum of [x,[y,z]] vanishes. In the affine extension the invariance of the bilinear form makes the central contributions satisfy this identity.

quote: the central term in (3.12) vanishes
preview: In the affine mode commutator the central term is the identity multiplied by ℓm times the pairing of x with y when m + n = 0. It vanishes for two strictly negative indices.

quote: The field of the zero state
preview: The state-to-field assignment is linear, so the zero state has the zero field and every coefficient of that field vanishes. In this example the constant coefficient includes a sum of mode products.

quote: This gives the finite negative Laurent tail
preview: On a fixed vector only finitely many negative powers can occur in a field. For a smooth affine module the high modes of every current kill that vector beyond a common bound that can vary with the vector.

quote: Translation equivariance alone gives
preview: The translation operator T kills the vacuum, and differentiating the field of a state a gives both the field of Ta and the commutator of T with the field of a. This describes translations in one coordinate.

quote: written for right differential modules
preview: On a smooth curve the right module associated to a left differential module M is the line of one-forms tensored with M. In a local frame dz the right action of ∂/∂z differentiates the M factor with a minus sign.

quote: The two-point chiral operation takes values
preview: This is a differential-module map from two inputs with poles allowed along the diagonal to an output supported on the diagonal. The output can retain derivatives in the separation of the two points.

quote: Place two Heisenberg currents at
preview: A rank-one Heisenberg current has modes Jₙ. At level κ, the commutator of Jₘ with Jₙ is κm times the identity when m+n=0 and vanishes otherwise.

quote: the third, the spectator, at
preview: A spectator is an insertion held at a separate position while the chosen pair collides. The resulting coefficient can still depend on its position and state.

quote: to the distinct open for
preview: Here the distinct open consists of tuples in which every two labelled points have different positions. With at least two labels it misses the small diagonal, so the target of the chiral operation restricts to zero there.

quote: is a right differential module
preview: A right differential module carries a right action of differential operators. On a smooth curve its local sections are densities dz ⊗ m, and right differentiation in z gives minus dz tensored with the covariant derivative of m.

quote: The chiral operation accepts precisely such Laurent multipliers.
preview: For right differential modules on a smooth curve, a chiral operation takes the external product of the inputs with collision poles allowed to a differential module pushed forward from the small diagonal. Its input therefore includes the Laurent multiplier.

quote: Near the small diagonal choose a local
preview: The small diagonal in the space of labelled positions is the locus where every position coincides. For three inputs it consists of the triples (x,x,x).

quote: the multiplication is homotopy associative on the fully localized source
preview: Here the two ternary composites have the same source and target. A degree −1 map m₃ has differential (ab)c − a(bc) in the mapping complex.

quote: the factorization identification on the block-separation open
preview: For a partition of the labels, this open consists of configurations in which points from different blocks have distinct positions. Points in the same block may coincide.

quote: to the category of unital Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebras
preview: On a smooth curve these are right differential modules with a skew chiral bracket satisfying Jacobi. The unit maps one-forms into the module and acts by the canonical residue operation.

quote: identifications on the word coefficients.
preview: On a smooth separated finite-type curve X over a characteristic-zero field, a word of length n carries a complex of right differential modules on Xⁿ. Extraordinary pullback identifies coefficients under adjacent repetitions, and the empty word has its own complex.

quote: of adjacent factors and, more generally, their associativity homotopies.
preview: On the suspended bar complex these operations are the components of a degree-one coderivation b with b²=0. In unsuspended degrees the n-input operation has degree 2−n, so the three-input operation has degree −1.

quote: The required factorization map for each
preview: For a cut of a word into a prefix and a suffix, restrict the coalgebra coproduct to the open where the two blocks are disjoint. Factorization requires this map to be an equivalence onto the external product of the two block coefficients.

quote: singleton configurations of the Ran space.
preview: The points of the Ran space are finite nonempty subsets of the curve. Tuples related by a permutation or repetition of labels describe the same subset.

quote: Applying associative cobar gives an associative chiral algebra of configuration complexes.
preview: For consecutive-cut convolution, this is an augmented coherently associative algebra with scalar empty coefficient. Its bar coalgebra must factorize across every consecutive cut.

quote: The scale circle acts by the full twist.
preview: A positive full twist rotates all points in one cluster once around their common centre while keeping the other clusters apart. Parallel transport around this loop acts on the coefficient fibre.

quote: so the link at the double collision vanishes.
preview: At this collision the normal link is the complex of cochains on the fully separated part of a small transverse neighbourhood, with its local coefficients. Both colliding pairs contribute to the same complex.

quote: Taking global sections of their homotopy fibres gives dimensions
preview: For each attaching map from the diagonal coefficient to the nearby cochains, its homotopy fibre is the cone of that map shifted by −1. It gives the complex of sections supported along the diagonal.

quote: A Gaussian Wilson ray carries a fixed charge to a boundary insertion.
preview: For a Gaussian abelian Wilson ray ending on the boundary, the charge is the eigenvalue of J₀ on its endpoint state. A positively oriented current contour divided by 2πi measures that eigenvalue.

quote: The quotients also agree off the origin. The attaching map
preview: The attaching map restricts the collision stalk to the cochains on a punctured neighbourhood. For these shifted four-ray quotients its image in degree −1 is the chosen line W.

quote: so the ordinary analytic monodromy is trivial for every
preview: Analytic continuation once around the puncture acts on the fibre of horizontal solutions. This loop action is the identity for every value of a in the triple-collision example.

quote: so a chain homotopy between them cannot exist
preview: For cochain maps f and g with the same source and target, a chain homotopy is a degree −1 map h with f−g = dh+hd. Such maps induce the same map on cohomology.

quote: For three ordered fields
preview: A field on a state space is an operator-valued Laurent series. On each fixed state only finitely many terms with negative powers of the coordinate survive.

quote: is a homotopy between these two maps.
preview: A homotopy comparing cochain maps g and f is a degree −1 map h with f−g = dh+hd. On three inputs the differential on the source uses the graded tensor rule.

quote: by the graded Leibniz rule. Since
preview: If a has even degree then d(ab) = (da)b + a(db). If a has odd degree the second term enters with a minus sign.

quote: The same choice of primitive enters the transfer
preview: A primitive of a boundary v is a cochain w one degree lower with dw=v. Two choices differ by a cycle, which can affect a transferred higher product.

quote: the augmentation ideal is one-dimensional and its product is zero.
preview: The augmentation ideal is the kernel of the unital algebra map to the ground field. For the dual numbers augmented by ε ↦ 0 it is spanned by ε, whose square is zero.

quote: Deconcatenation expresses this requirement.
preview: Deconcatenation sends a word to the sum of its prefix tensored with its suffix over all cut positions. The two end cuts contribute an empty word.

quote: The nonzero Massey coset measures
preview: For the three closed degree-one generators choose dx=ab and dy=bc. The class of ay+xc is taken modulo [a]H¹(A)+H¹(A)[c], which accounts for changing the two primitives.

quote: Conilpotence makes the word sum finite on each element.
preview: In a coaugmented coalgebra, conilpotence means that sufficiently many iterations of the reduced coproduct kill each element of the coaugmentation coideal. The required number may depend on the element.

quote: the twisting-cochain adjunction is
preview: For a conilpotent coaugmented dg coalgebra C and an augmented dg algebra A, a degree-one twisting cochain C → A specifies both a dg algebra map ΩC → A and a dg coalgebra map C → BA. This is the strict adjunction with Ω on the left.

quote: is an entire coderivation, which can act in several word lengths.
preview: A degree-one coderivation b obeys Δb = (b⊗1 + 1⊗b)Δ with graded tensor signs. A single coefficient of the deformation can act on several lengths of suspended words.

quote: calls for the homotopy fibre of the restriction map.
preview: Over a specified action, a point of this fibre consists of a lift and a path from its restricted action to the specified one. The fibre retains the higher compatibilities of these choices.

quote: A factorizing coproduct identifies the two-letter term
preview: On a separating open, the cut coproduct identifies the restricted coalgebra coefficient with the external product of the coefficients of the two blocks. In arity two each block consists of one label.

quote: On each cut open the coproduct must split
preview: For a cut after position p, every position in the prefix must be distinct from every position in the suffix. Either block can still have internal collisions.

quote: The same definition of an associative chiral algebra can be used with the symmetric convolution
preview: For convolution on the full ordered collision atlas, this is an augmented coherently associative algebra with zero empty coefficient in its augmentation ideal. The bar coproduct must factorize on the separating open for each ordered bipartition.

quote: Indeed the binary cobar differential uses a map
preview: In cobar the differential uses the internal differential of a desuspended coalgebra coefficient and splits that coefficient by its reduced coproduct. For the two-label ordered atlas the split has two components, one for each ordering.

quote: for the chiral tensor on the full Ran space,
preview: The Ran space uses all nonempty finite sets of labels, their relabellings and their collisions. At the level of points, repetitions give the same finite subset of the curve.

quote: recovers every mode. For
preview: The mth mode sends b to the residue of uᵐY(a,u)b du. Allowing negative m also recovers the coefficients of the regular powers of u.

quote: has the normal links calculated in
preview: For a finite-rank local system in degree zero on the fully distinct complex configurations, the normal link at a collision is the cochain complex on the separated part of a small transverse neighbourhood. A cut open can have a different separated part.

quote: on the whole Spencer complex.
preview: The Spencer complex adds an exterior tangent of degree −1 for each label. Its differential contracts a tangent with the corresponding covariant derivative, including translation on the field coefficient.

quote: this is the counit.
preview: For the graded opposite of the derived endomorphism algebra of W, induction of RHom(W,M) has an evaluation map to M. On degree-zero inputs it sends w ⊗ f to f(w). Being an equivalence tests recovery of M.

quote: generated by a vector killed by the strictly positive current modes.
preview: These are the modes x tʳ for x in the finite Lie algebra and r ≥ 1. They kill the inducing vector of W, while its lowest-energy states form the regular module for the zero modes.

quote: at a complex shifted level outside
preview: The shifted level is the raw affine level plus the dual Coxeter number, with long roots of squared length two. In this chapter the shifted level is s = −k.

quote: modules by inverting quasi-isomorphisms.
preview: A quasi-isomorphism is a chain map inducing an isomorphism on cohomology in every degree. The ordinary derived category makes each such map invertible.

quote: Derived tensor and derived Hom give an adjunction
preview: Maps from ΦL to M correspond naturally to maps from L to ΨM. For these derived functors the correspondence is an equivalence of mapping complexes.

quote: For a strictly augmented dg bialgebra
preview: A bialgebra has a coassociative coproduct and a counit that respect multiplication and the unit. In the differential graded setting these are chain maps.

quote: If \(F\) is compact as an \(H\)-module
preview: A module is compact in a derived category if maps from it commute with arbitrary direct sums. Here compactness of the trivial module lets the invariants functor preserve those sums.

quote: Mapping complexes are formed at a specified homogeneous shift
preview: A map of cochain degree r has a component from each degree n to n + r, so these components form a product. Here the energy shift is fixed first, and the sum over energy shifts is algebraic.

quote: Under the smooth realization hypotheses,
preview: The inducing object must carry its prescribed right B-action in the smooth derived category, with compatible Taylor cutoffs and the homogeneous endomorphism comparison. Derived tensor and smooth Hom must give the specified adjunction.

quote: The restricted dual with arbitrary vector-space coefficients
preview: Take the ordinary linear dual of each finite-dimensional degree of the positive-current enveloping algebra, then take the direct sum. Each functional is supported in finitely many degrees.

quote: take a smooth K-injective replacement
preview: This is a quasi-isomorphism to a complex J such that Hom(X, J) is acyclic for every acyclic X in the smooth module category. It computes derived Hom even for unbounded complexes.

quote: is K-flat on both
preview: Tensoring with a K-flat module takes acyclic complexes of modules on the opposite side to acyclic complexes. Here B must have that property over R on both sides.

quote: Its map out of \(L\) is the scalar-extension unit
preview: This sends L to its derived tensor with R over B, viewed again as a B-module. On a resolution the map takes v to 1 ⊗ v.
